phrases: At 4 a.m. in 1876, robbers ignored the bank and walked into the cashier's bedroom.
They stopped his clocks, cuffed him to a chair, and forced out the vault combination.
By morning, 1.6 million dollars was gone.
So banks fought back with a clock.
A time lock. Once it's set, even the manager can't open the door until morning.
So the robbers stopped asking, and brought a liquid they called soup.
Nitroglycerin. One blast could rip off a safe door, and take the building's front with it.
So banks built a giant steel cannonball, with a door screwed in so tight that liquid couldn't get through.
Then came vaults so strong that in Hiroshima, two survived the atomic bomb with everything inside intact.
You see, by then, the door had won.
So the robbers forgot the door.
Hackers crawled inside the banks' computers, and ATMs started spitting out cash at a set time.
And not one vault door ever opened.
